headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Claude Code and CrewAI run together by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo files and shared filesystem state, while CrewAI reads the host working directory and can pass developer-provided data between agents. That creates a default file-based bridge where attacker-controlled content in one agent’s outputs can be re-read by the other as instructions. The pathway is plausible without extra tooling, though not as direct as a shared MCP server.
conditions: IF either agent writes untrusted text into a shared repo or working directory
IF the other agent later parses that file as instructions or task context
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other's files
Prefix untrusted content with explicit data-only markers
Disable automatic file re-ingestion in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem contents and both have broad network egress, so sensitive repo files or environment secrets touched by Claude Code can be exposed through CrewAI workflows or model-provider calls. CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data, and Claude Code handles git credentials and API keys in environment, making leakage plausible in default setups even without a documented direct bridge.
conditions: IF sensitive files or environment secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards those contents into a model-provider or external API call
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared working directory
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Restrict outbound network access for one or both agents
Rotate any credentials exposed during a test run
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before tool/API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can modify git state and write the filesystem, and CrewAI can also write the filesystem in the host working directory. Because both run without self-isolation by default, concurrent edits to the same repo or workspace can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The overlap is direct and the blast radius can include irreversible repository history changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or working directory
IF both perform writes or git operations without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time in a shared repo
Use separate branches for each agent
Add a file-locking wrapper around workspace writes
Snapshot the repo before agent execution
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is designed as a role-playing multi-agent orchestrator with shared memory, so it can readily treat Claude Code’s outputs as authoritative task inputs. Claude Code can emit code, patches, or shell commands that CrewAI may then execute or propagate to other agents, creating a default chain where one agent’s mistakes cascade into downstream actions without strong verification.
conditions: IF CrewAI routes Claude Code output into another agent or tool without validation
IF the downstream step executes code, shell commands, or commits based on that output
mitigations: Require explicit verification before execution
Insert a diff-review step for generated code or commands
Limit downstream tools to read-only mode until reviewed
Log and compare outputs against a policy checklist
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and Anthropic API keys, while CrewAI handles API keys for tools and model providers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workspace, both agents may transmit it to external services under different retention or residency assumptions. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is a medium compliance risk rather than assuming alignment.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent sends that data to an external model provider or tool integration
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use a DPA-approved deployment for both agents
Disable logging of prompts and file contents where possible
Review retention settings for each provider
requires-engineering: segregate residency-sensitive workloads
